note: Routes that cannot be driven by any gauntlet tier today. Every entry names WHY and WHO. A route with no entry and no observation appears in the report's 'NO stated reason at all' row, which is the row that should make someone uncomfortable. 'No tier drives it yet' is a real and admissible reason; it is deliberately NOT phrased as 'blocked' when nothing structural prevents it, so that a missing test never launders itself into an external blocker. Rules: most specific matching rule wins; a trailing '*' is a prefix glob; keep an entry only while it is true, and delete it the moment its route executes. Every entry also carries a `class`, and tools/genref/generate.mjs refuses this file if one is missing or unknown, because the register's honest never-executed figure is a sum over two of these classes. out-of-release-set: no tier deploys the program at all. structural: genuinely undrivable at HEAD, and the entry argues why. repointing: not a block -- the entry redirects a reader, or records one already discharged. unwired: the route IS driven today and emits no census evidence, which is a wiring defect and not a protocol one. status-report: no campaign or tier drives it yet, and nothing structural is in the way. The last two are the classes that count as never-executed however carefully they are worded, because a sentence in this file is not an execution.

blocked.reason: The Dealer arm of dclutch-accelerator-sbf (formerly dclutch-dealer-accelerator-sbf, folded 2026-09-04; its refusals now sub-band 0xC100). Driven today by programs/dclutch-accelerator-sbf/dealer-program-test (12,062 lines, the accepted/frontier/physical suites over the real ELF), which emits no census evidence and has no bindings, so the two set_return_data arms read as never executed. The accelerator ELF itself is deployed and Registry-pinned beside the seven roles (general_accelerator.* in the cohort manifest), so the old out-of-release-set reason no longer holds for this arm; what is missing is evidence wiring and a runner, exactly the dealer-checkpoint shape. Cohort-17's scoring Dealer replaces the selector-9 evaluation this arm hosts (MECHANISM_SCORING_DEALER section 2, section 6). Previous entry, kept for its history: Dealer accelerator, not part of the seven-role successor release set; no tier deploys it. THE FRAME-CLEANLINESS HALF OF THIS ROW IS RESOLVED (W2h, 2026-08-27): measured at c3c4950 and again at 5e25f8e, cargo build-sbf on programs/dclutch-dealer-accelerator-sbf emits ZERO 'overwrites values in the frame' diagnostics, against 253 measured on the same tree at the immediately preceding HEAD. TA-DLR's root cause was correct and is independent of the fix: with `no-entrypoint` set, dclutch-trading-sbf compiles without its own #[global_allocator], which leaves __rust_alloc an opaque extern that cannot be folded at its call sites and spills hot_v3::process_hot_execution_v3 past the SBPF v0 4,096-byte frame. What changed is the headroom, not the allocator: process_hot_execution_v3 used 3,904 bytes of that frame with the outgoing-argument area filling the rest, and c3c4950 split it into an authentication half (3,008 bytes) and an execution half (2,496), which absorbs the opaque extern. TA-DLR's two-edit patch is therefore NOT required for this row and is NOT applied. It remains the principled fix for the underlying incoherence -- a no-entrypoint library build of Trading still runs Hot code under whichever allocator its host executable installs, not the one the shipped Trading program uses -- and if it is taken: re-measure on top of c3c4950 rather than against the stale 253; land both halves together (either alone is a duplicate or a missing #[global_allocator], both hard errors); and per W1f keep admit_heap_frame_v1 and lift_declared_heap_profile_v1 reachable in the SHIPPED ELF, where DCLTPCB1 depends on them on chain now. Widening the cfg does not move the shipped build either way, since `no-entrypoint` is off there and both predicates already evaluate the same. The emitted accelerator .so was never contaminated in any case: process_hot_execution_v3 is dead-stripped from it.

blocked.reason: The Series arm of dclutch-accelerator-sbf (folded 2026-09-04; sub-band 0xC200). No campaign has driven a Shadow request against a deployed accelerator: the Consume act's ShadowAot strategy is selected by the V5 release and its seven strategy extras are assembled and authenticated by crates/dclutch-operator/src/series_current_acquisition_v5.rs, and the successor verb that would carry it (local-private-validator-series-terminal-consume-v1) drives the lifecycle planner through series_terminal_campaign::run_with_policy. THE ARM ITSELF NOW EXECUTES, natively: series::process refuses InvalidInvocation 0xC200 when the common Shadow callback cannot authenticate the invocation (an_unauthenticated_callback_refuses_in_this_programs_own_band, CONVERGE-SERIES 2026-09-06), which is the first execution of this arm in any language; the same commit gives that collapse its msg!, because one accelerator code stood for four distinct Trading causes with nothing on the refusing path to say which. TWO facts still stand between the ELF and its first CHAIN execution, and only one of them was named before. (a) The Shadow certificate's artifact binding -- and the BUILD-SERIES seam named the wrong site: the generator does not AUTHOR a certificate, it carries the identity its source manifest states (generator/src/manifest.rs, CERTIFICATE_IDENTITY; build_series_shadow_source_v1 reads input.checked_release.certificate), and the only in-tree writer of a Series certificate identity is series_shadow_lab_include, which takes one on the command line and says of itself that it is not release evidence. joined_artifacts.rs:251 is the GENERAL authoring site, not a Series one. So no in-tree producer authors a Series certificate at all, of either binding; the acquisition admits both and is tested doing so (the_acquisition_admits_both_certificate_bindings_and_swaps_neither). (b) The campaign that verb drives reads an input of schema dclutch-owned-loopback-series-terminal-campaign-input-v2 whose seven acquisition recipes, two market retirements and current-source corpus NOTHING IN THIS TREE WRITES: SeriesHotAcquisitionRecipeV2 is declared once, as a Deserialize-only reader inside the campaign. A driver over an input with no producer is not a driver. RULING (BUILD-SERIES, provisional): a Series Shadow certificate binds the accelerator's source-derived semantic_release_id (CertificateArtifactBindingV2::Semantic), never the ELF digest, so it can be authored before the ELF that embeds it exists; the ELF digest is bound by the Registry ArtifactReleaseV1 the activation cache names and by the Loader ProgramData check at callback time (shadow_accelerator_auth::deployment). The acquisition admits both bindings; the generator's include still authors a Release binding and is the seam (programs/dclutch-accelerator-sbf/generator/src/lib.rs, source.release_sources.certificate).

It was 'no chain carries a live V1'; RELEASE-DEVNET falsified that on 2026-09-01 (cohort-9's core carries a live 144-byte V1 at FYzxwAjEqRwzYA727p3K3bCyEioesJoCQzx6oKVeVmNe, so conjunct 2 is satisfied) and it became conjunct 4: infrastructure_v2.rs refuses a succession in which nothing moved, and a cohort deployed hours ago has moved nothing. c60b25e8 then changed what the route MEANS. Since 2951b226 every Core route authenticates the V2 profile only, so a genesis cohort could never found -- measured on cohort-9, which reached activation and refused its founding sixty transactions deep. The repair was NOT a V1 fallback in the readers (PROFILE_UPGRADE_RULING_2026_08_31 section 6 refuses try-V2-then-V1 by name, and while that refusal's benefit analysis went stale the parallel-authority failure it named did not): process_initialize now commits a GENESIS V2 alongside the V1, using two distinct domain-separated sentinels as predecessor ids, so there is still exactly one authentication path. Conjunct 6 became ONE SUCCESSION PER DOMAIN rather than one V2 per domain, reading those sentinels -- a born-at-V2 profile has not spent its succession, a profile naming real V1 artifact releases has. So this route is no longer the thing that makes a cohort foundable; it is now only what a cohort needs to MOVE its Registry. It stays undrivable until a cohort carries a born-at-V2 profile and makes a real Loader-v3 upgrade to a strictly later deployment slot -- which needs the cohort-10 redeploy that carries c60b25e8, since this is a program change and reaches chain no other way. Cohort-9 cannot host it: its Core predates the genesis arm and its V2 PDA G5M2jgBQXypkUgoMc2jswH8WZx61ykDcSeQm3Bfw5tTF was read back as an untouched vacancy. Manufacturing the forward slot by re-uploading identical Registry bytes is a ceremony performed on the check and was refused. Consent still needs the PREDECESSOR release's bound upgrade authority to sign, so a cohort revoking authority on both infrastructure roles is permanently unfoundable -- 6155219a refuses that at plan time by name. Evidence: docs/evidence/COHORT9_DEVNET_DEPLOY_2026_09_01.md. NOTHING may report the ceremony as executed until it actually runs.

blocked.reason: THE OBSTACLE IS THE LAB'S CLOCK ARITHMETIC, AND IT IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED. Everything else this route needed exists and has been exercised on a live validator by `tools/gauntlet/ladder`: the two-source market compiles through the shipped `--recovery-rungs` parser, the founding publishes its `RecoveryPolicyV2`, and the shipped `advance-recovery` driver builds the relay contract's own 18-account frame and refuses a too-early crank BY NAME with no key open. What no bounded lab run can reach is the second the crank becomes admissible. A loopback market's primary leg is due at `window.end + max_age`; `window.end` IS the captured fixture publication (`fixtures/pyth/local-upgraded-2026-08-22`, publish time 1787431680) and `FIXTURE_SHELF_LIFE_SECONDS` is one year, so the primary leg of every loopback market -- and therefore every rung anchored on it -- falls in August 2027. The ladder tier founded one and its crank reported the leg due 30,406,xxx seconds away and refused, which is the driver behaving correctly against a market nothing can walk. THE FIX IS ONE FIELD, AND IT LANDED WITH THE CONVERGENCE (2026-09-04): `LocalMarketShapeV1.terminal_max_age_seconds`, a caller-stated primary shelf life (default `None` = the fixture's own, so every existing caller compiles byte-identically), threaded into `max_age_seconds` and into `authored_relative_ladder_v1`'s anchor, with a `--terminal-max-age-seconds` flag on the loopback market command. That is the honest alternative to warping a validator's clock, and it is no more of a lab setting than the constant it replaces: a frozen publication's staleness grows by 86,400 every day and is a fact about the LAB. MEASURED UNDER EXACTLY THAT PATCH on 2026-09-04, in a private worktree, on one loopback validator: the route executes twice. The primary leg was due at 1788572039 and the crank landed at 1788572040 -- ONE SECOND after, which is the strictness itself -- writing RecoveryAdvanced for 204,690 CU over an 18-account frame, and the Source read back phase Recovery attempt 0. The rung's own committed deadline was 1788572159 and the second crank landed at 1788572160 for 197,216 CU, and the Source read back Exhausted. Each was refused by name first -- 761 and 115 seconds early, no key open, nothing sent. For comparison the real-ELF program-test figures are advance 216,637 / exhaust 218,163; these are single loopback draws with fresh keypairs and bump-search noise in them. WHAT THE PATCH DOES NOT BUY IS A RUNG CAPTURE. One `max_age` governs both the crank's admissibility and the publication's freshness, so a shelf life short enough for the primary leg to close inside a lab run is one under which the frozen publication is already stale for every rung after it. A rung answered on a loopback needs a publication the lab can refresh -- a fixture question, not a wiring one.

blocked.reason: NO CAMPAIGN, and the driver is COMPLETE -- this is a binding gap, not a missing executor. `execute_split_market_founding` (tools/local-validator/bootstrap/successor/src/market.rs) drives DCLTGFP1 then DCLTGMO1 with four hostiles (stage interleaving, a substituted Claims request, a wrong permit, a permit replay), and as of 2026-09-04 it is selected by `MarketRunInput::founding_route` rather than by an environment variable nothing set. It is not a parallel authority to the atomic route: same codec, same Core dispatch, one prestate prologue shared up to the founding submission itself. WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY RIDE TIER 1, which is the part worth writing down: a split run makes three of tier 1's own files wrong at once. Its two `DCLTGMF3` bindings would match no transaction, and a binding that matched nothing is a hard census error; six of its CU_BUDGETS rows key on the atomic label, and a budget matching no transaction is red; and its witnesses query `.label | startswith("DCLTGMF3 refuses")`. So a split campaign is a TIER, in the sense TIERS.md means: its own directory, its own bindings merged with tier 1's shared prefix at run time the way journey/ does it, its own witnesses, and its own CU_BUDGETS campaign name with numbers measured from its first completing run -- plus `SuccessorRunSpec::founding_route`, which exists, to select the route for tier 1's compiled fixture. Nothing structural is in the way; the work is a campaign nobody has written.
